executiveSummary: Analysis of 20 surveillance reports from ECDC and PAHO spanning November 2025 through May 2026 reveals multiple concurrent public health threats across the Americas and Europe. Avian Influenza A(H5N1), a BSL-3 select agent, has generated multiple epidemiological updates for the Americas region, indicating sustained zoonotic transmission risk. Mpox, dengue, measles, and pertussis are all experiencing notable activity in the Americas, while ECDC weekly threat reports signal ongoing European communicable disease concerns. The convergence of respiratory virus season onset in the Southern Hemisphere with persistent arboviral and vaccine-preventable disease outbreaks represents a complex, multi-threat landscape requiring coordinated surveillance.
bottomLine: Multiple simultaneous public health threats across the Americas and Europe—led by H5N1 zoonotic spillover risk and resurgent vaccine-preventable diseases—demand heightened surveillance and cross-regional coordination.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Multiple PAHO epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained circulation
Zoonotic spillover events in the Americas with animal-to-human transmission risk
BSL-3 select agent with pandemic potential requiring high-containment protocols
Sustained animal reservoir activity necessitating repeated alerts over 4-month period
threats.action: Activate enhanced zoonotic surveillance at animal-human interfaces; enforce PPE protocols for exposed workers; sequence all human cases; coordinate with FAO/OIE on animal sector response and pre-pandemic vaccine stockpiling

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued April 2026 indicating active transmission
BSL-3 select agent with person-to-person transmission capacity
Ongoing circulation requiring dedicated regional alert within 2026 surveillance period
Potential for clade expansion or severity changes warranting close genomic monitoring
threats.action: Enhance contact tracing and ring vaccination; conduct clade-specific genomic surveillance; strengthen diagnostic capacity in affected countries; coordinate cross-border case notification

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued February 2026 indicating elevated case burden
Americas region historically experiences hyperendemic dengue with severe case potential
Early 2026 alert timing suggests inter-epidemic surge or serotype shift
Concurrent Chikungunya alert suggests shared Aedes vector driving co-transmission
threats.action: Intensify vector control operations; expand serotype surveillance to detect serotype shifts; strengthen severe dengue case management; issue travel advisories for high-burden areas

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza and RSV
threats.pathogen: Influenza A/B viruses; Respiratory Syncytial Virus
signals: PAHO alert issued April 2026 marking Southern Hemisphere season start
Simultaneous RSV and influenza co-circulation alert issued January 2026
ECDC weekly threat reports across April-May 2026 indicating Northern Hemisphere ongoing activity
Co-circulation increases healthcare system burden and complicates clinical differentiation
threats.action: Promote vaccination uptake for influenza and RSV-eligible populations; reinforce hospital surge capacity; enhance sentinel surveillance for severity indicators; cross-reference ECDC and PAHO data for hemispheric tracking

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two separate PAHO alerts issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained resurgence
Multi-month alert persistence suggests ongoing epidemic rather than isolated outbreak
Vaccine-preventable disease resurgence may reflect immunization coverage gaps
Risk to unvaccinated infants and immunocompromised populations is significant
threats.action: Audit vaccination coverage rates by country and district; implement catch-up immunization campaigns; strengthen neonatal cocooning strategies; investigate potential waning immunity in adolescent cohorts

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 indicating active transmission
Americas region had achieved measles elimination status, making resurgence a public health emergency
Vaccine-preventable resurgence signals critical immunization coverage gaps
High transmissibility (R0 12-18) enables rapid spread in under-vaccinated communities
threats.action: Conduct emergency supplemental immunization activities; investigate coverage gaps and vaccine hesitancy drivers; implement rapid outbreak response protocols; verify elimination status in affected countries

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued March 2026 indicating active cases or spillover risk
BSL-3 pathogen with high case fatality rate in unvaccinated individuals
Alert timing suggests epizoonotic activity in sylvatic cycle with human spillover risk
Travel-related export risk to non-endemic regions with susceptible populations
threats.action: Ensure vaccination coverage in at-risk populations and travelers; strengthen epizoological surveillance in primate populations; review international traveler vaccination requirements; pre-position medical countermeasures in high-risk zones

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 indicating active transmission
Co-circulation with dengue via shared Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus vectors
Arboviral alert cluster in early 2026 suggests vector season amplification
Risk of new geographic expansion into previously unaffected territories
threats.action: Integrate chikungunya surveillance into existing arboviral monitoring platforms; strengthen vector control in co-endemic areas; improve clinical differentiation from dengue; monitor for geographic spread into new regions

selectAgentSummary: Two BSL-3 select agents have been identified in active surveillance reports: (1) Avian Influenza A(H5N1) — flagged as Critical threat with multiple PAHO updates across November 2025 and March 2026, indicating sustained zoonotic activity in the Americas with pandemic spillover potential; (2) Mpox virus (MPXV) — flagged as Elevated threat with a dedicated PAHO update in April 2026, confirming active transmission in the Americas region. Yellow fever virus, also a BSL-3 pathogen, is flagged as Elevated based on a March 2026 PAHO alert indicating active human spillover risk. All three require high-containment diagnostic protocols and immediate public health response measures.
amrSignals: Bordetella pertussis macrolide resistance potential warrants monitoring given sustained resurgence despite vaccination and antibiotic prophylaxis programs
Influenza antiviral resistance (oseltamivir) should be surveilled given high H5N1 and seasonal influenza activity across both hemispheres
No direct AMR reports in available report titles, but ECDC weekly threat reports may contain unspecified AMR signals requiring full-text review
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous resurgence of multiple vaccine-preventable diseases (measles, pertussis) across the Americas in early 2026 suggests systemic immunization coverage erosion, potentially pandemic-era legacy
Co-circulation of multiple arboviruses (dengue, chikungunya, yellow fever) in early 2026 indicates amplified Aedes vector season, possibly driven by El Niño-related climate conditions
H5N1 generating alerts in both November 2025 and March 2026 suggests enzootic establishment in Americas animal reservoirs rather than isolated incursion events
Convergence of Southern Hemisphere influenza season start (April 2026) with ongoing respiratory RSV co-circulation creates compounded healthcare system burden risk
ECDC issuing consecutive weekly threat reports through April-May 2026 (weeks 16-20) indicates sustained elevated communicable disease pressure in Europe without apparent resolution
GLP-1 receptor agonist medication misuse alert from PAHO (February 2026) represents an emerging non-infectious public health threat intersecting with healthcare system capacity
